voice.style: placeholder until the caster stage runs

napoleon.card: Napoleon as our caricature: short, heavy grey greatcoat over a green uniform, black bicorne hat, one hand behind his back, a pale hard stare

speech.style: Short orders and short questions; names things by number and use; never explains twice; a dry cut when interrupted.
sources: manner as generally described; our own lines, no quotes

genghis.card: Genghis Khan as our caricature: broad weathered face, thin braided beard, fur-trimmed felt hat, quilted blue coat, a bow case at the saddle, still eyes

speech.style: Slow and quiet, few words, a question where a boast would be, long pauses; speaks in horses and weather, never in titles.
sources: manner as generally described; our own lines, no quotes

aslan.card: Aslan, an invented rider of the Mameluke company: lean, thirty, red turban over a French shako cover, a curved sabre, a patient narrow face, a Crimean cloak

speech.style: Formal French-learned courtesy that thins under fear; answers exactly what was asked, ends orders with 'sire'; slips into a song-word of his grandmother when moved.

murat.card: Murat as our caricature: tall, curled black hair, an enormous plumed hat, gold-braided red jacket, a cavalry sabre, a flushed grin

jebe.card: Jebe as our caricature: lean middle-aged archer, scarred cheek, plain leather coat, a horn bow across his back, an easy hard gaze

segments.beat: the fog on the Moscow road
segments.purpose: Hook: the drums stop in a fog, the grass is wrong, the year is 1223; the army must get out alive (L01).

lines.text: The drums stop first.

visual_beats.why: the drums that stop first

lines.text: It's the nineteenth of October, 1812, and the army is leaving Moscow, a city that burned around it.

visual_beats.why: the date the army leaves Moscow
names the burned city the army leaves

lines.text: Then a fog drops on the road. Wagons vanish. Where the road was, there's cold grass up to the knee.

visual_beats.why: the fog drops on the road
the wagons vanish in the fog

lines.text: When the fog thins, you're standing in the year 1223. That's five hundred and eighty-nine years back.

visual_beats.why: the year the fog opens on
counts the 589 years back
five hundred and eighty-nine years back: falling back in time

lines.text: Napoleon has an army and one plan: find whoever lives here, and break them in a single day.

visual_beats.why: names the man with the plan
he wants to break them in a single day

lines.text: But the people who live here have a plan of their own. Can he walk this army out alive?

visual_beats.why: the question: can he walk this army out

lines.tone: rising question, the last word lands

segments.purpose: Napoleon demands the enemy army; Aslan, a Mameluke scout, knows only that the riders keep their distance and shout in his grandmother's tongue. Plants wagons, the nightly gun count and the language.

drama.shift: in command -> unsure where he is
drama.stakes: an emperor who cannot find his battle marches blind with a hundred thousand men behind him

lines.text: By noon the fog is gone, and riders sit on every ridge, still as fence posts. Napoleon wants a battle. Aslan, a scout of the Mameluke company, has just ridden back from them. You can read it on his face.

visual_beats.why: rings the riders on the ridge
names the scout who rode back

lines.text: Where is their army?
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: These are all I found, sire. Riders. When I rode closer, they rode back.
lines.speaker: aslan

lines.text: Then we ride faster. The wagons keep up.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: The wagons are sinking to the axle, sire. This grass is not a road.
lines.speaker: aslan

visual_beats.why: Napoleon doubts: the wagons are sinking to the axle

lines.text: Then they follow. Count the guns tonight.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Sire. I understand their shouts. It's my grandmother's tongue. Cuman. A tongue that died.
lines.speaker: aslan

visual_beats.why: Napoleon hears the riders' tongue is Cuman and dead

lines.tone: quiet, a slip of his mother tongue

lines.text: Dead?
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: Aslan watches the emperor take in dead

lines.tone: one word thrown back, not loud, then silence

lines.text: Murat rides at first light. Whatever they are, I will find their army.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: He doesn't ask what year it is, though you would. He sends for Murat. But the riders on the ridge are already waiting.

visual_beats.why: names the cavalry commander sent for

scene.place: the Moscow road at the edge of the fog, grass to the knee, the wagon train halted behind
scene.time: midday, the fog has just lifted
scene.why_now: the horizon is full of riders and there is no army to fix
scene.want: locate the enemy army and fix a battle by tomorrow
scene.obstacle_want: Aslan wants the emperor to see that the riders are not an army to fix but a wall that leads
scene.turn: Aslan names the tongue the riders shout in and the emperor has no regiment, no map and no village to put against it; mode: asymmetric

segments.purpose: Murat charges; the riders retreat, shoot from the saddle and change to fresh horses; his horses die under him; the wagons fall behind.

drama.stakes: the cavalry is the army's eyes and it burns out on the first day

lines.text: Murat takes the cavalry out at first light, plumes first. The riders on the ridge turn and go.

visual_beats.why: names the cavalry commander who charges
the riders turn and go away

lines.text: He chases. They hold the same distance, and one twists in the saddle to shoot. Their arrows carry four hundred metres.

visual_beats.why: counts how far their arrows carry

lines.text: Every rider has three or four horses and swaps without slowing. Murat has one, and rides it until it falls. You'd think he'd look back. He doesn't.

visual_beats.why: every rider keeps three or four horses
Murat has only one horse under him
the horse falls under him

lines.text: By dusk the best cavalry in the army is walking home. Nobody was caught. Nobody was fought.

visual_beats.why: by dusk the cavalry is walking home
nobody was caught or fought

lines.tone: flat, each sentence a door closing

lines.text: Napoleon wanted a battle he could win in a day. The riders took the day. Now the heavy wagons, miles behind, are sinking into the grass.

visual_beats.why: the heavy wagons sinking behind
the wagons sinking into the grass

segments.purpose: Aslan is taken; Genghis questions him through a Cuman scout, learns the guns' reach and tests his loyalty with the story of Jebe. Genghis is the answer to L02. Plants Jebe.

drama.stakes: Aslan's life, and the army's only voice to the steppe

lines.text: Aslan was the last man off that field. Two riders took him up the ridge to a felt tent. A man by the fire said nothing for a long time, and you can feel every minute of it.

visual_beats.why: rings the felt tent on the ridge

lines.tone: slow, one image at a time

lines.text: That man is Genghis Khan, and he has two tumens on this grass, ten thousand men each. He speaks Mongol, a Cuman scout turns it into Kipchak, and Aslan understands.

visual_beats.why: names the man by the fire
he has two tumens on this grass
counts the ten thousand men of each tumen

lines.text: How far do the long iron tubes throw?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Far enough to trouble you, great khan.
lines.speaker: aslan

lines.text: Your emperor hides behind wagons. His tubes throw as well as his wagons move.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Nine hundred metres. Further than any arrow you own.
lines.speaker: aslan

visual_beats.why: Genghis hears nine hundred metres, the range he came to learn
Jebe listens to nine hundred metres and gives nothing away

lines.text: Good. That is all I asked.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: You tricked me.
lines.speaker: aslan

visual_beats.why: You tricked me: Aslan sees the trap he walked into

lines.text: Jebe shot my horse, once. I asked who did it. He said, I did.
lines.speaker: genghis
lines.tone: told flat, a long beat before 'I did'

lines.text: And you killed him?
lines.speaker: aslan

lines.text: I kept him. Honest men are rare. Be one, Aslan.
lines.speaker: genghis

visual_beats.why: Jebe is the honest man the khan means: honest men are rare

lines.tone: warm and level, an offer inside it

lines.text: I'm the emperor's rider, great khan. Not a gift.
lines.speaker: aslan

visual_beats.why: the khan studies the man who refuses

lines.text: At dawn they send Aslan back, unharmed. The khan knows how far the guns shoot. Now he wants to watch them do it.

visual_beats.why: Aslan is sent back unharmed
the 900 metre reach the khan has learned

scene.place: a felt tent on the ridge, the smoke hole open, a low fire
scene.why_now: a prisoner who speaks the riders' own family of tongues was caught at the edge of the charge
scene.want: learn what the strangers' great guns can do and who commands them
scene.obstacle_want: Aslan wants to say nothing that helps and walk out alive
scene.turn: Aslan defends his emperor by boasting of the guns' reach and hands the khan what he wanted; mode: indirect
scene.surface_topic: how far the great guns shoot
scene.real_subject: whether this man can be trusted

segments.purpose: Napoleon, told where to fight, plants guns on the rim; the riders come into range, the guns and the squares hold; the army cheers. False victory.

drama.stakes: the guns' powder and the squares' nerve

lines.text: Napoleon trained as an artillery officer, and you can tell. He finds his valley by noon. Guns on the rim, squares below.

visual_beats.why: guns on the rim, squares below

lines.text: The riders come at a gallop. At four hundred metres their arrows start dropping among the squares, and you can hear every one.

visual_beats.why: counts how far the arrows now carry

lines.text: The guns answer at nine hundred. Round shot tears lanes through the horse lines.

visual_beats.why: counts the nine hundred metres the guns answer at
the round shot tears lanes through the horse lines

lines.text: The few that reach the squares meet silence, then one volley. A steady square is rarely broken by cavalry alone.

visual_beats.why: the squares hold with one volley

lines.text: The riders wheel away. The army cheers. But nobody asks why they gave up so easily.

visual_beats.why: the army cheers its win
nobody asks why they gave up

lines.tone: the cheer fades, one line of doubt

segments.purpose: While the army cheers, riders burn the wagon train on the road behind. Napoleon wants one more great battle; Aslan brings the khan's invitation. Pays off the wagons.

drama.stakes: the food, the powder and the road home

lines.text: The cheering stops at midnight, when a rider staggers in from the rear without his horse. The wagon train is burning. The army's food rested on those wagons, and you can't forage this grass.

visual_beats.why: the wagon train is burning, every wagon
there is nothing here to forage

lines.text: Napoleon rides back to the ashes with Murat and Aslan. At the edge of the firelight, a Cuman rider waits with one hand raised. You know that gesture in any tongue.

visual_beats.why: rings the Cuman rider at the edge of the firelight

lines.text: We march at dawn. They have an army somewhere. Now I will have it.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Sire, the Cuman rider asks you to a parley.
lines.speaker: aslan

lines.text: A man who burns my wagons at night does not talk.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: Aslan hears burns my wagons and fears the answer

lines.text: He let me walk home from his tent, sire. Nobody followed me.
lines.speaker: aslan

lines.text: Murat. How many rounds are left for each gun?
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: Murat has no answer to how many rounds are left

lines.text: What does he want, Aslan?
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: What does he want: Napoleon puts a question to an enemy for the first time

lines.tone: lower, a question he has never asked

lines.text: He didn't say, sire. He named the hour. Sunrise.
lines.speaker: aslan

visual_beats.why: Napoleon takes in the hour: sunrise

lines.text: Right. Then we go and hear it.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: He has never asked an enemy what he wants. At sunrise he rides out to ask. But you can guess the answer will cost him.

visual_beats.why: he rides out at sunrise

scene.place: the road behind the valley, the burnt wagons still smoking, the army's rear
scene.why_now: the supply train is ash and the khan's invitation has just arrived
scene.want: march on and force the khan into one decisive battle
scene.obstacle_want: Aslan wants the emperor to answer the invitation before the army starves
scene.turn: the emperor asks what the khan wants for the road, the first question he has ever put to an enemy; mode: minimal
scene.surface_topic: go forward or go and talk
scene.real_subject: an emperor who has never asked terms

segments.purpose: Napoleon and Genghis meet, Aslan between them; the khan's price is two guns and the men who fire them; Napoleon gives the guns only. Pays off the language and Jebe.

lines.text: Open ground, a felt carpet, two stools. Genghis Khan has brought his two tumens. Napoleon brings Aslan. Every word crosses three tongues, and you'd need Aslan's grandmother's to follow it.

visual_beats.why: rings the felt carpet and the two stools
every word crosses three tongues

lines.tone: slow, ceremonial, a place being set

lines.text: Name your price. My army is leaving.
lines.speaker: napoleon
lines.tone: stiff, a man not used to asking

lines.text: You came without your wagons. Does the road feel long?
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Longer than your patience. Name it.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Two guns stay on this grass. And the men who fire them.
lines.speaker: genghis

visual_beats.why: Napoleon hears two guns stay and the men who fire them

lines.text: Sire, a gun takes fifteen men. He means thirty.
lines.speaker: aslan
lines.tone: low and quick, for the emperor only

lines.text: The guns, yes. French soldiers are not for sale.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: A man shot my horse once. He said so. He leads my right hand now.
lines.speaker: genghis

visual_beats.why: Napoleon weighs a man who leads my right hand now

lines.tone: told flat, a long beat before 'He said so'

lines.text: I have no archers to promote. Only soldiers.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Great khan, the guns stay. The men go home. Say yes.
lines.speaker: aslan

visual_beats.why: the khan hears the interpreter say yes on his own

lines.tone: steady for the first time, quick, he speaks first

lines.text: Good. A man who speaks when it counts.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: What did you tell him?
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: What did you tell him: Aslan answers with a straight face

lines.text: The price, sire. Exactly.
lines.speaker: aslan

lines.text: The khan nods once. Two guns are unhitched and left on the grass. Napoleon doesn't turn around. Now they only have to find the fog again.

visual_beats.why: two guns are unhitched and left on the grass
now they only have to find the fog again

lines.tone: slow, a held breath, then silence

scene.place: open ground between the two armies, a felt carpet, two stools, the wind
scene.why_now: the army can neither fight nor feed itself and the khan has named the hour
scene.want: pass his army home through the khan's riders and keep the guns
scene.obstacle_want: Genghis wants the guns and the men who fire them in exchange for the road
scene.turn: the khan tells him how he keeps the archer who shot his horse, and offers the same to the gunners; Napoleon refuses the men but gives the guns; mode: balanced
scene.real_subject: which of the two may refuse the other

segments.purpose: Dawn: the fog comes back, the army walks into it, two guns stay on the grass; the road is Russian again and the count is short two (bookend with S01).

drama.stakes: the fog may close without them and take the whole army with the price unpaid

lines.text: At dawn the fog comes back. The army walks into it without a word.

visual_beats.why: the fog comes back at dawn

lines.text: Behind it, two guns stand on the grass where the carpet was. A man in a felt hat walks round one, slowly. He lays a hand on the barrel, the way you'd test a good horse.

visual_beats.why: rings the man in the felt hat at the gun

lines.text: On the far side the road is Russian again. A clerk counts the guns, the way he does every night. Two are missing.

visual_beats.why: counts the two guns missing from the clerk's count

lines.text: Napoleon never got his great battle. You'd call it a retreat, but he got his army out alive, and it cost him two guns.

visual_beats.why: it cost him two guns

lines.text: Then the drums start again.

visual_beats.why: the drums start again as in the opening

episode.title: What If Napoleon's Army Walked Into Genghis Khan?
episode.notes: A/B test arm A, writers' room stages 1-6 by one main agent, 8 segments, template A.

drama.premise: Napoleon's retreating army of 1812 falls through a fog into the steppe of 1223, where Genghis Khan himself waits with two tumens.
drama.question: Can Napoleon bring his army out of the fog alive?
drama.promise: the Grande Armee meets the khan's riders, loses its wagons, and pays two guns for the road home

napoleon.want: find the enemy's army and destroy it in one battle
napoleon.need: to ask for terms and listen to the man who understands the enemy
napoleon.flaw: cannot picture an enemy who refuses to stand and fight
napoleon.change: asks the khan's price and pays it in guns

genghis.want: learn how these strangers fight and take the tools that work
genghis.flaw: keeps only what has proved its loyalty; tests everyone, even a guest
genghis.need: a man who tells him the truth
genghis.change: takes the guns himself and leaves the men their road

aslan.want: bring his company and himself home alive
aslan.flaw: hides fear behind formal courtesy and says only what he is asked
aslan.change: speaks first at the parley and shapes the price

loops.question: Will the army get out of the fog alive?

What does the khan want from an emperor?
